How it works

Three steps, and a report you can argue with.

No connection to either platform. Drop in the export you already have and read the reconciliation before you decide to trust it.

01

Read the source

Tableau XML, Qlik script or a Cognos spec is parsed into one addressable model — joins, lineage and all.

02

Translate and map

Calculations become DAX, checked against your knowledge base first. Mark types resolve to Power BI visuals.

03

Reconcile

Every object counted in and counted out, scored against your gate, and the shortfall named object by object.

The honest part

Four things it will not do.

Each is reported as a named loss rather than quietly approximated.

Qlik SECTION ACCESS

Emitted as an empty RLS role with the original rule in a comment. Someone rebuilds and tests it.

R and Python scripts

No DAX equivalent exists. The measure becomes a placeholder and is listed as unsupported.

Table-calc addressing

WINDOW_ and RUNNING_ translate structurally, but partitioning rarely survives. Always flagged.

Pixel-exact layout

Pages, visuals and bindings carry. Fonts, spacing and floating containers land close, not identical.

Start with one workbook.

Drop in a .twbx, a .qvf or a Cognos export. It runs in this tab, uploads nothing, and hands you the reconciliation report first.
